# Results -- Study 177 (Megacap-Concentration) on real data

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe -- each January,
rank all S&P 500 names by **prior year-end** market cap (EDGAR diluted shares x yfinance
year-end close), hold the top-10 (or top-7) equally weighted for the full calendar year,
and compare vs the equal-weight baseline and SPY total return. No look-ahead: the ranking
uses prior-year data. As-of **2026-06-15**. Universe = current S&P 500 members
(survivorship-biased -- all returns are upper bounds on investable performance).*

## Data stamp

| Source | Coverage | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| EDGAR `WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding` | 2007-2026, 412 tickers | (repo cache, shared) |
| yfinance year-end closes (`auto_adjust=True`) | 2007-01-01 -- 2025-12-31 | `b6555c5c4c43` |
| SPY total return | 2008-2025 | shared `_cache/SPY_total_return.parquet` |

Complete years used: **18** (2008-2025, excluding partial 2026). Top-10 concentration
strategy -- 18 annual holding periods across 412 (survivorship-biased) names.

**Survivorship bias caveat:** the universe is today's S&P 500 members. Companies that
went bankrupt, were acquired, or were delisted between 2008-2025 are missing. This
inflates all return estimates. A real fund would have held names like Bear Stearns,
Lehman Brothers, or Sears at some point -- none of which appear here.

## Full-sample results (2008-2025, 18 years)

### Top-10 concentration vs equal-weight

| Arm | n years | mean ann. return | excess vs EW | HAC t-stat | ann. Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Top-10 (lagged mcap rank)** | 18 | **+15.0%** | **-1.6 ppt** | **-0.31** | **0.57** |
| Equal-weight (all names) | 18 | +16.6% | — | — | — |

The top-10 concentration strategy **underperforms** the equal-weight S&P 500 by
**1.6 ppt/year** over the full sample (HAC t = -0.31 -- statistically noise, but the
point estimate is negative).

### Top-7 concentration vs equal-weight

| Arm | n years | mean ann. return | excess vs EW | HAC t-stat | ann. Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Top-7 (lagged mcap rank)** | 18 | **+13.7%** | **-2.9 ppt** | **-0.58** | **0.54** |
| Equal-weight (all names) | 18 | +16.6% | — | — | — |

Top-7 is even worse: -2.9 ppt/year, t = -0.58. Greater concentration makes the
recency-bias problem larger, not smaller.

### vs SPY total return

| Arm | excess vs SPY | HAC t-stat |
|---|--:|--:|
| Top-10 vs SPY | +2.4 ppt/yr | +0.58 |

Slight positive vs SPY (which includes dividends, while the top-10 is price-return
only -- the comparison is conservative for the concentration strategy), but not
statistically significant.

## Decade split -- the regime flip

This is the most important result: the claim holds in one specific era and fails badly
in two others.

| Period | n years | Top-10 mean | EW mean | Excess | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Pre-2015** (2008-2014) | 7 | **+2.4%** | **+16.5%** | **-14.0 ppt** | **-10.27** |
| **2015-2019** | 5 | **+16.6%** | **+16.3%** | **+0.3 ppt** | **+0.11** |
| **Post-2020** (2020-2025) | 6 | **+28.3%** | **+17.0%** | **+11.3 ppt** | **+1.30** |

- **Pre-2015:** megacaps lost by **14 ppt/year**, HAC t = **-10.3**. The size premium
  was alive and punishing the largest names. The top-10 included names like Citigroup
  (-77% in 2008), GE (declining for a decade), and IBM (secular underperformer).
- **2015-2019:** flat, near-zero excess (FAANG era beginning, but not yet dominant).
- **Post-2020:** megacaps won by **+11.3 ppt/year** (Nvidia +239%, +121%; Apple, Microsoft,
  Google strong), but t = **+1.30** -- not statistically significant on just 6 years.
  The Magnificent-Seven era is real in the data, but insufficient to overturn 14 years
  of prior underperformance.

## Synthetic positive control

The engine correctly recovers a concentration advantage when one is planted: at
`effect=0.10` (10 ppt annual alpha for top-10 stocks over 50 simulated years), the
excess return is +11 ppt/year with t > 9. At `effect=0.0` the excess is indistinguishable
from zero. The real-tape result (-1.6 ppt) is therefore a statement about the data, not
the method.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- MIXED.** The claim "megacaps always win" fails over the full 2008-2025
  history (-1.6 ppt, t=-0.31). It fails catastrophically pre-2015 (-14 ppt, t=-10.3).
  It succeeds post-2020 (+11.3 ppt) but with only 6 years and t=+1.30. The honest
  verdict is MIXED: the claim holds in one specific regime, not as a general rule.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** The strategy is survivorship-biased (inflated returns),
  regime-dependent (14 years of underperformance before 2020), and offers no stable
  signal across the full history. An investor launching in 2008 on the "biggest companies
  are best" logic would have earned ~2.4%/year through 2014 while the average stock
  earned ~16.5%.
- **Recency bias -- CONFIRMED.** The 2020-2025 Magnificent-Seven era is a genuine
  performance window, but extrapolating 6 years of exceptional returns onto a general
  "megacap concentration always wins" claim requires ignoring 14 years of contrary evidence.
